Article Title: TSMC and Taiwan researchers engineered an interface only 0.42 nanometers thick to improve next-generation MoS2 transistors
Article Text:
Representational AI photo

Focus on Atomic Boundary

Why interface matters

Science Daily photo

0.42-nanometre buffer layer

Relevance for future chips

Researchers from Taiwan's National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (NYCU) and TSMC Corporate Research have developed a new way to improve transistors made from atomically thin materials. They focuses on the tiny boundary where two materials meet, which allowed them to build transistors with an extremely thin insulating layer while maintaining strong electrical performance.According to Science Daily, atomically thin semiconductors have been studied for more than a decade because some can be just one atom thick while still showing useful electrical properties. Such materials could allow transistors to become smaller, faster and more energy efficient than conventional silicon-based devices.However, making these very thin transistors work well has been difficult. One major problem involves the gate dielectric, an extremely thin insulating layer that helps control the movement of electrons. Making it thinner can improve transistor control, but when it is placed on an atomically thin semiconductor, problems can develop at the boundary between the two materials. These can interfere with electron movement and reduce performance.The new study, published in Nature Electronics, addresses this problem by engineering the atomic interface between the semiconductor and the insulating layer.The NYCU team worked with TSMC Corporate Research to engineer the narrow region where the two materials meet. Instead of focusing only on finding a new semiconductor, the researchers changed the interface itself.The team used monolayer molybdenum disulfide, or MoS2, as the semiconductor. A monolayer is a material that is only one layer of atoms thick. The researchers first placed an ultrathin epitaxial aluminium layer directly on the MoS2.They then oxidised the aluminium to create an aluminium oxide layer about 0.42 nanometres thick. After this, they added a high-κ hafnium oxide gate dielectric, an insulating material that can provide strong electrical control while remaining very thin.The 0.42-nanometre aluminium oxide layer acted as a buffer between the MoS2 and hafnium oxide. It created a smoother surface, helping the hafnium oxide grow more uniformly, while also reducing unwanted electrical interactions between the two materials."For many years, efforts to improve atomically thin transistors have largely focused on discovering better semiconductor materials," said Professor Wen-Hao Chang, the study's corresponding author from NYCU. "Our research shows that the atomic interface between materials can be just as important. By engineering that boundary, we were able to reduce one of the fundamental trade-offs that has limited two-dimensional transistors for many years," he added.Atomically thin semiconductors create a particular challenge because their surfaces do not have dangling bonds. This makes it difficult to grow an extremely thin dielectric layer evenly across the surface.Standard deposition methods can leave gaps and defects at the interface. These can create electrical disorder and reduce carrier mobility, which refers to how easily electrons move through a material.Researchers have explored different dielectric materials, molecular seed layers and other oxide deposition methods. However, achieving a very thin equivalent oxide thickness, strong electrostatic control and high carrier mobility at the same time remains difficult.The challenge is especially important for wafer-scale CVD-grown monolayer MoS2. CVD, or chemical vapour deposition, is a method used to produce thin material layers over a larger area.The researchers' approach was to redesign the interface rather than replace the semiconductor or gate dielectric. They placed the ultrathin epitaxial aluminium layer on monolayer MoS2 and oxidised it to produce the 0.42-nanometre aluminium oxide layer. The high-κ hafnium oxide was then added on top.The team built short-channel top-gate transistors using CVD-grown monolayer MoS2. The devices had an equivalent oxide thickness of about one nanometre.Tests showed low leakage current and minimal hysteresis. Hysteresis refers to unwanted differences in a transistor's electrical response depending on its previous operating condition.The transistors reached a maximum transconductance of 0.45 mS μm-1, with channel lengths of about 100 nanometres. Transconductance measures how strongly a transistor's current responds when the gate voltage changes.The devices combined a very thin dielectric with strong electrical control and continued carrier transport, a combination that has been difficult to achieve in atomically thin transistors.The findings highlight the growing importance of interfaces as transistor components become smaller. When materials are only a few atomic layers thick, the region where two materials meet can strongly affect how the device performs."When transistor components become only a few atomic layers thick, the interface is no longer simply the boundary between materials, it becomes an active part of the device," said Professor Tsung-En Lee, the study's corresponding author. "Learning to engineer these interfaces with atomic precision opens new opportunities for designing future semiconductor devices that would be difficult to achieve by changing individual materials alone," professor Lee added.The researchers believe the approach could contribute to future two-dimensional electronics. Using CVD-grown monolayer MoS2 also brings the work closer to materials and processes that could eventually be considered for wafer-scale manufacturing.
Article Summary: Researchers from Taiwan's National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University have developed a new way to improve transistors made from atomically thin materials. They focuses on the tiny boundary where two materials meet, which allowed them to build transistors with an extremely thin insulating layer.

Article Title: Why US is questioning Pakistan's Rs 3 trillion defence spending
Article Text:
The US also criticised Islamabad for not publishing its executive budget proposal within a reasonable period (representative image)

US asks Pakistan to improve defence and debt transparency

Pakistan's defence allocation rises to Rs 3 trillion

Defence spending remains a key transparency concern

The US state department has flagged a lack of adequate parliamentary and civilian oversight of Pakistan's military and intelligence spending, while also raising concerns over limited disclosure of government debt and delays in publishing the executive budget proposal.The concerns were highlighted in the 2026 Fiscal Transparency Report, which assessed Pakistan's public financial transparency and identified gaps in the country's budgetary and fiscal disclosure practices.The report noted that Pakistan made its enacted budget and end-of-year financial statements widely available online. However, it said military and intelligence budgets remained outside adequate parliamentary or civilian public scrutiny.“The military and intelligence budgets were not subject to adequate parliamentary or civilian public oversight,” the report said.The US also criticised Islamabad for not publishing its executive budget proposal within a reasonable period.According to the assessment, this limits the time available for lawmakers and civil society to examine government spending before the budget is adopted.The state department called for three key changes to Pakistan's fiscal transparency framework.It urged Islamabad to make its executive budget proposal publicly available within a reasonable period, disclose detailed information about government debt obligations, including liabilities linked to state-owned enterprises, and bring military and intelligence agency budgets under parliamentary or civilian public oversight.The report also raised concerns about Pakistan's disclosure of public debt, saying only limited information was available on debt obligations, including those of major state-owned enterprises.At the same time, the US assessment acknowledged some positive aspects of Pakistan's public financial system.It said the country's supreme audit institution met international standards of independence and noted that its audit reports were published in a timely manner and contained substantive findings.The US assessment comes against the backdrop of a substantial increase in Pakistan's defence allocation for the 2026-27 financial year.In June, Pakistan's federal government proposed allocating Rs 3 trillion for defence services, up 17.65 per cent from the previous year's initial allocation of Rs 2.55 trillion, according to Dawn.The proposed defence services allocation amounts to about 2.08 per cent of Pakistan's projected GDP of Rs 143.6 trillion and nearly 16 per cent of the federal government's total outlay of Rs 18.77 trillion.Spending on civil works related to military infrastructure was projected to rise 7.92 per cent to Rs 363.16 billion, from Rs 336.49 billion previously.Military pensions are accounted for separately from the main defence services budget. The government has allocated Rs 822 billion for retired military personnel under the federal pension outlay, according to Dawn.The allocation for defence administration was set at Rs 10.9 billion, compared with Rs 7.9 billion in the outgoing fiscal year's original budget. That allocation was later revised to Rs 11.75 billion.Major military imports and defence acquisitions are generally funded outside the main defence services allocation and remain undisclosed.The US state department's assessment therefore highlights a distinction between Pakistan's publicly disclosed defence allocation and the wider military spending that may not be fully visible through the country's budgetary documents.The state department's recommendations focus on bringing military and intelligence expenditure into the broader framework of public financial oversight.While the report recognised that Pakistan publishes key budget documents, it identified defence and intelligence spending, debt disclosure and the timing of budget publication as areas requiring greater transparency.The recommendations would require Pakistan to give lawmakers and the public greater visibility into military and intelligence allocations, as well as government liabilities linked to state-owned enterprises.
Article Summary: US asks Pakistan to improve defence and debt transparency. Pakistan's defence allocation rises to Rs 3 trillion for 2026-27 financial year. US state department flagged a lack of adequate parliamentary and civilian oversight of Pakistan's military and intelligence spending. Report also raised concerns over limited disclosure of government debt and delays in publishing executive budget proposal.

Article Title: Indian national Nikhil Gupta's sentencing in Gurpatwant Pannun murder plot case delayed to November 20
Article Text:
Gurpatwant Pannun murder plot case delayed to November 20.

Gupta pleaded guilty to three charges

A US federal court has delayed the sentencing of Nikhil Gupta, who pleaded guilty to plotting to assassinate Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun to November 20, according to court filings.Gupta's sentencing was originally scheduled for September 25 before the US District Court for the Southern District of New York. The hearing was postponed after the alleged intended victim requested more time to attend and speak at the sentencing, PTI reported, citing court filings.The victim was not named in the court filings. However, Pannun's lawyer has publicly identified him as the target of the alleged murder-for-hire plot.In a letter filed before the US District Court for the Southern District of New York, federal prosecutors said the unnamed victim "wishes to participate in the sentencing" and requested that the September 25 hearing be adjourned."The Government respectfully requests the Court grant a brief adjournment to effectuate the victim’s statutory rights to attend and be heard at the sentencing," prosecutors said in the letter.The prosecutors added that Gupta’s defence team had no objection to the postponement and was available on November 6 or November 20. Judge Victor Marrero granted the request and rescheduled Gupta’s sentencing for November 20 at 10 am.Also read: Nikhil Gupta, Pannun murder plot and the Nijjar connection: Inside a case that spanned 3 continents Gupta pleaded guilty on February 13 to all three charges against him, murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering, in connection with the alleged plot to kill Pannun.The murder-for-hire and conspiracy charges each carry a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, while the money-laundering conspiracy charge carries a maximum sentence of 20 years.Gupta was arrested in the Czech Republic on June 30, 2023, and extradited to the US a year later. US prosecutors have accused Gupta of arranging to pay $100,000 to a hitman to assassinate Pannun, a dual US-Canadian citizen.The alleged plot was reportedly carried out at the direction of an Indian government official identified by US authorities as Vikash Yadav.The plot was disrupted after the person Gupta believed to be a hitman turned out to be an undercover US federal agent. According to the US Department of Justice, Yadav allegedly recruited Gupta in May 2023 to help coordinate the planned killing of Pannun in New York.Gupta's sentencing will now take place on November 20, when the court is expected to hear from the intended victim as part of the sentencing proceedings.
Article Summary: Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty to plotting to assassinate Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. Gupta's sentencing was originally scheduled for September 25 before the US District Court for the Southern District of New York. The hearing was postponed after the alleged intended victim requested more time to attend and speak.

Article Title: Russia kills at least 10 in Ukraine as Zelenskyy accuses Moscow of using North Korean missiles
Article Text:
Firefighters work at a compound of a warehouse hit by an overnight missile strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv, Ukraine

Zelenskyy warns of further Russian escalation

Russian strikes damage Kyiv children's hospital, steel plant

Ukraine strikes Russian oil facilities

UN says more than 16,000 Ukrainian civilians remain detained

At least 10 civilians were killed in Russian missile, drone and glide-bomb attacks across Ukraine on Tuesday, Ukrainian officials said, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of using North Korean ballistic missiles and preparing for further military escalation.Zelenskyy said Russian forces used ballistic missiles supplied by North Korea in an overnight strike on Zaporizhzhia in southeastern Ukraine. Seven workers at a steel plant were killed and 21 others injured in the attack, according to the company operating the facility.Three more people, including a 15-year-old boy, were killed by Russian drones and artillery in the central Dnipropetrovsk region, officials said.The latest strikes came as Zelenskyy said North Korea was preparing to deploy additional troops to Russia.Moscow and Pyongyang have significantly expanded military cooperation since Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un signed a strategic partnership agreement in 2024, which includes a commitment to provide mutual assistance if either country faces aggression.North Korea has already sent thousands of troops and large quantities of weapons to support Russia's war in Ukraine, according to Ukrainian officials and Western assessments.Zelenskyy said Russia was increasing ballistic missile production while continuing to receive military support from North Korea.“Every step Russia takes — increasing ballistic missile production, bringing in North Korean equipment, preparing for mobilisation — all of this shows that Moscow is preparing not for peace, but for escalation,” he said on social media.Ukraine has warned that Russia is seeking to exploit its shortage of Patriot air-defence interceptors, which are among the systems capable of countering ballistic missiles.The Institute for the Study of War, a Washington-based think tank, said Ukraine's shortage of Patriot interceptors could allow Russia to cause significant damage over the coming winter and potentially contribute to prolonging the war.The think tank also assessed that the Kremlin was unlikely to make meaningful compromises in negotiations as long as Russian President Vladimir Putin believed Moscow had a viable military path towards achieving its objectives.US-led diplomatic efforts to end the war have made little progress, while Washington's attention has also been focused on the conflict involving Iran.Russian forces also struck Kyiv overnight. One strike hit the grounds of a children's hospital, creating two craters and shattering windows, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service.Children and medical workers were sheltering underground and nobody was injured in the attack, officials said.Another strike started a fire at a warehouse in Kyiv that spread across around 1,200 square metres, emergency officials said.The Russian defence ministry said its forces had targeted “military industrial facilities and transport and logistics centers” in Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia using ground-based precision weapons. It claimed that civilian storage facilities containing drones in Kyiv and a metallurgical plant in Zaporizhzhia were among the targets.Ukraine's air force said Russia used Zircon anti-ship missiles and Iskander ballistic missiles against Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia, along with 120 long-range attack drones.The air force did not provide its usual daily figure for the total number of missiles launched, and it was not immediately clear why.Metinvest, a major Ukrainian mining and metals company, said seven employees at its steel plant in Zaporizhzhia were killed while attempting to reach shelters after an incoming ballistic missile warning.The company said the attack damaged a blast furnace and other equipment, forcing the plant to halt operations.The escalation came alongside Ukrainian attacks on Russian territory.Russia's defence ministry said its air defences intercepted nearly 400 Ukrainian drones over 14 regions and Crimea overnight.Ukraine's General Staff said its forces also struck an oil refinery in Orsk in Russia's Orenburg region, around 1,500 km from Ukraine. The refinery has an annual crude-processing capacity of about 44 million barrels and produces fuels including gasoline, diesel and aviation fuel. The extent of the damage was being assessed.Separately, Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian energy infrastructure in recent months, targeting oil refineries as part of efforts to put pressure on Moscow.In another attack, at least 12 people were killed and 39 injured in a Ukrainian drone strike on industrial and civilian targets in Nizhnekamsk in Russia's Tatarstan region, according to the city's mayor.The attack also hit the TANECO oil refinery, one of Russia's major refining facilities. The region declared a period of mourning following the attack.The United Nations meanwhile said more than 16,000 Ukrainian civilians detained by Russia during the war remained deprived of their liberty.Claudia Fuentes Julio, the UN assistant secretary-general for human rights, told an informal UN Security Council meeting that many detainees were being held incommunicado and on grounds that did not comply with international law.She also said “widespread and systematic torture and ill-treatment” of Ukrainian civilian detainees and prisoners of war by Russia was continuing, including sexual violence.The latest Russian strikes and Ukrainian attacks come as the war enters its fifth year, with diplomatic efforts to secure a settlement showing little progress and both sides continuing to expand their long-range strike capabilities.
Article Summary: Russian forces used ballistic missiles supplied by North Korea in an overnight strike on Zaporizhzhia in southeastern Ukraine. Seven workers at a steel plant were killed and 21 others injured in the attack. Three more people, including a 15-year-old boy, were killed by Russian drones and artillery in the central Dnipropetrovsk region.

Article Title: From fast fashion to fast repairs: Clothing brands push in-store mending to draw GenZ
Article Text:
A clothing repair workshop at a Levi’s retail store in San Francisco

NEW YORK: Encouraging customers to mend worn clothes instead of buying new ones might seem like a self-defeating sales strategy. But in-store repairs and sewing workshops are becoming essential retail services for clothing brands as they try to appeal to young consumers who want to save money and the planet.While luxury fashion houses and select specialty retailers like Patagonia have offered product repairs for decades, the concept has caught on. Jeans giant Levi Strauss & Co., casual wear chain Uniqlo and budget retailer Primark are some of the apparel companies hoping to win over Generation Z shoppers with a needle and thread.Levi's created a handstitching course for high school students after determining that many Gen Zers lacked the sewing skills to match their interest in thrift store shopping and sustainability. Employees spend 90 minutes instructing teenagers on four tasks: sewing on a button, hemming, patching a hole and fixing a tear.The Wear Longer programme, which the San Francisco-based company is expanding across the, US builds on the repair and customisation services Levi's offers at hundreds of stores worldwide. "We think it's important to empower the people who buy our clothes with the skill sets to maintain them, to get them to that second life," Paul Dillinger, Levi's head of global design innovation, said.The evolution of mending from an economic necessity and traditional craft to a method for cultivating customers didn't happen overnight. The fashion industry as a whole has come under intensifying pressure to reduce its contributions to environmental pollution and climate change.Researchers broadly agree that repairing and reselling clothes can reduce a garment's environmental impact, especially if it delays or replaces a new purchase. But many caution the practices remain too limited to offset continued growth in clothing production and consumption.Clothing production roughly doubled between 2000 and 2015, while the average number of wearings per garment declined by 36%, according to the Ellen MacArthur Foundation. The sustainability nonprofit estimated that less than 1% of discarded clothing material got recycled into new apparel.Enter Generation Z, born between 1997 and 2012. It's the generation that grew up with fast fashion and e-commerce, then had school years and young adulthoods shaped by the coronavirus pandemic and post-pandemic inflation. Whether due to limited budgets or a rejection of materialism, Gen Z has helped the pre-owned clothing market grow much faster than retail apparel sales in the US, independent market intelligence firm GlobalData estimated in a report with resale platform ThredUp.The question facing the industry is whether repairs can evolve from niche service to commercially viable. Sweden's H&M Group, which has presence in over 80 countries, has been candid about one of the biggest obstacles: the economics. The company has argued that repair and resale are desirable goals, but manufacturing new garments costs less than keeping existing ones in use. Making mending work in retail is challenging as it's labour intensive and must be priced low enough to entice customers, Saunders, of GlobalData, said. AP
Article Summary: Levi's created a handstitching course for high school students after determining that many Gen Zers lacked the sewing skills to match their interest in thrift store shopping. Jeans giant Levi Strauss & Co., casual wear chain Uniqlo and budget retailer Primark are some of the apparel companies hoping to win over Generation Z shoppers.

Article Title: North Korea Ballistic Missile Launch: North Korea fires second ballistic missile in a week ahead of US-South Korea war drills
Article Text:
A TV screen shows a file image of North Korea's missile launch during a news program at Seoul Railway Station (Picture credit: AP)

Seoul, Tokyo condemn launch

Second reported launch since August 6

Pyongyang continues to expand missile arsenal

North Korea fired a ballistic missile towards the sea off the Korean Peninsula’s east coast on Wednesday, South Korean and Japanese authorities said, marking Pyongyang’s second reported ballistic missile launch in less than a week and coming days before major US-South Korea military exercises.South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missile was launched from the Wonsan area on the North’s eastern coast at around 6 am (local time) and travelled more than 700 km (435 miles).Japan’s defence ministry also detected the launch and said the missile landed in waters outside Japan’s exclusive economic zone (EEZ), between the Korean Peninsula and Japan.Japan said the missile reached a maximum altitude of about 90 km (56 miles.The latest launch came two days after South Korea and the United States announced that their annual Ulchi Freedom Shield military exercises would begin on August 17.The drills are scheduled to run until August 27 and are aimed at strengthening readiness against North Korea’s nuclear and missile threats.North Korea has repeatedly condemned the exercises, describing them as rehearsals for an invasion. The United States and South Korea have maintained that their military training is defensive.South Korea’s National Security Council held an emergency meeting following the launch and described North Korea’s continued ballistic missile tests as acts of provocation. It urged Pyongyang to stop activities that violate UN Security Council resolutions.South Korea’s military said it remained prepared to respond to any provocation under its combined defence posture with the United States.According to Reuters, the military said it would respond “overwhelmingly” if necessary.Japan also lodged a protest with North Korea through diplomatic channels.“It’s a serious problem that affects the safety of the Japanese people,” Japanese defence minister Shinjiro Koizumi told reporters.Japan’s defence ministry said the missile landed outside its EEZ. Koizumi said Tokyo had “strongly condemned” the launch.There was no immediate statement from Pyongyang on Wednesday’s launch.The launch follows another reported ballistic missile test on August 6, when South Korea, the United States and Japan detected a short-range ballistic missile launched by North Korea.That was the North’s first reported ballistic weapons test since late June. North Korea did not immediately confirm that launch, although Pyongyang often releases details of weapons tests a day after they take place.The latest launches come amid a broader continuation of North Korea’s weapons-testing programme. The country has conducted tests involving short-range ballistic missiles, artillery rockets and other tactical weapons this year.Experts cited by news agency AP said North Korea has often used US-South Korean military exercises as a pretext to increase its own weapons testing.UN Security Council resolutions prohibit North Korea from conducting ballistic missile launches.However, Pyongyang has continued developing its missile and nuclear capabilities, particularly since diplomatic efforts between North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and then-US President Donald Trump broke down in 2019.North Korea has since expanded its weapons arsenal and testing programme. Experts say Kim may seek to use the expanded capabilities to strengthen his negotiating position with Washington, including in any future discussions over sanctions.The latest test also comes as North Korea continues to strengthen its ties with Russia and China.North Korea has supplied troops and ammunition to support Russia’s war in Ukraine, while relations with China have also received renewed attention.Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Pyongyang in June, his first visit to the North Korean capital in seven years.
Article Summary: Second reported launch since August 6 and comes days before major US-South Korea military exercises. South Korea’s National Security Council held an emergency meeting following the launch. It urged Pyongyang to stop activities that violate UN Security Council resolutions. Pyongyang has continued developing its missile and nuclear capabilities, particularly since diplomatic efforts between North Korea and then-US President Donald Trump broke down in 2019.

Article Title: Trump's move to curb birthright citizenship faces legal challenge
Article Text:
The American Civil Liberties Union and other immigration advocacy groups filed the challenge to Trump's new executive action before a New Hampshire federal judge

Bloomberg

President Donald Trump's latest move to restrict automatic citizenship is facing a legal challenge, months after the Supreme Court knocked down his earlier attempt at upending longstanding guarantees for children born in the US to non-citizens.Lawyers who defeated Trump's original curbs on birthright citizenship asked a judge on Tuesday to declare that one of two executive orders the president signed on Aug 6 violates an existing injunction. That court order currently bars the administration from denying the status to babies whose mothers have temporary visas or who are undocumented migrants in the US illegally.The American Civil Liberties Union and other immigration advocacy groups filed the challenge to Trump's new executive action before a New Hampshire federal judge, who had approved that case as a class action. "If the president issues 100 orders seeking to create new exceptions to the sacred guarantee of the Citizenship Clause, all 100 will be equally illegal," the lawyers wrote. "The court should make clear that defendants may not take away class members' birthright under the auspices of these or any other executive actions. "
Article Summary: Lawyers who defeated Trump's original curbs on birthright citizenship asked a judge on Tuesday to declare that one of two executive orders the president signed on Aug 6 violates an existing injunction. That court order currently bars the administration from denying the status to babies whose mothers have temporary visas or who are undocumented migrants in the US illegally.

Article Title: Indian-origin ex-CFO of US firm gets 4-month jail term for bribing surgeons with sham consulting fees
Article Text:
Aditya Humad, a former CFO of SpineFrontier Inc. will serve four months in prison. (Representative image)

An Indian-origin former chief financial officer of a US spinal implant company has been sentenced to four months in prison for bribing surgeons to use the company's products in exchange for sham consulting fees, authorities said.Aditya Humad, 41, a Cambridge resident and former CFO of SpineFrontier Inc., will serve four months in prison, followed by one year of supervised release, and pay a USD 9,500 fine.Humad had earlier pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to violate the federal anti-kickback statute. He was charged in September 2021 along with Kingsley R Chin, SpineFrontier's founder, president and CEO.According to the US Attorney's Office for the District of Massachusetts, Humad conspired to pay and direct the payment of more than USD 540,000 in bribes to surgeons through sham consulting fees for work they did not perform.The payments were intended to induce surgeons to use SpineFrontier's spinal products during surgeries. The company, in turn, generated millions of dollars in revenue from procedures performed by the surgeons, authorities said.“This sentence is the culmination of years of dogged pursuit of SpineFrontier, its executives, Aditya Humad and Kingsley Chin, and multiple bribe-taking doctors,” United States Attorney Leah B Foley said, according to news agency PTI.Foley said Humad had been convicted and sentenced for conspiring to pay bribes to physicians to induce them to use the company's products in complicated spine surgeries.“In criminal and civil proceedings, we have recovered more than USD four million from these executives, their companies and the physicians who took their bribes. Let these resolutions serve as notice that no matter how long it takes, and how sophisticated the scheme, we will crack down on health care fraud offences,” Foley added.Authorities said Humad and SpineFrontier entered into contracts with surgeons that purportedly paid between USD 250 and USD 1,000 an hour for technical feedback on the company's products.Prosecutors, however, said the consulting arrangements were used to facilitate payments to surgeons in exchange for using SpineFrontier products in surgeries, including procedures covered by Medicare, Medicaid and the Veterans Health Administration.The surgeons often spent only a small portion of the hours they reported, if any, performing actual consulting work, prosecutors said.SpineFrontier subsequently received millions of dollars in revenue from surgeries performed by the doctors, according to authorities.“This corporate scheme sought to corruptly influence surgeons by paying hundreds of thousands of dollars in bribes to induce the use of SpineFrontier’s medical devices in surgeries,” Roberto Coviello, special agent in charge at the US Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG), the agency reported. Coviello said Humad's actions undermined safeguards intended to protect patients and the integrity of taxpayer-funded healthcare programmes.
Article Summary: Aditya Humad, 41, a Cambridge resident and former CFO of SpineFrontier Inc. will serve four months in prison, followed by one year of supervised release, and pay a USD 9,500 fine. Humad had earlier pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to violate the federal anti-kickback statute. He was charged in September 2021 along with Kingsley R Chin, the company's founder, president and CEO.

Article Title: Catering cart & military aircraft: How Trump secretly moved out of Turkey amid Iran assassination threat
Article Text:
President Donald Trump speaks while switching planes at US Air Force Base RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk Eastern England, on his way back to Washington from the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey. (AP/PTI image)

Poll Vote & Share your view What measure do you think can help reduce conflicts between countries? Diplomatic talks and negotiations International mediation and cooperation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

US President Donald Trump was secretly moved in an airport catering truck to a smaller military aircraft after boarding Air Force One in Ankara, a covert operation triggered by an Iranian assassination threat, The Washington Post reported Monday.Trump had initially boarded the older, baby-blue Air Force One in front of cameras after attending the Nato summit in Turkey.But after getting on the aircraft, he was secretly shuttled by an airport catering truck to an Air Force C-32A, which then flew him to Britain, the Post reported, citing a US official familiar with the operation and corroborating material it reviewed.The extraordinary security operation came as hostilities with Iran were escalating. Iran borders Turkey, where Trump had travelled for the Nato summit and made his first international trip aboard a newly renovated jet donated by Qatar.The president's unexpected switch from the new aircraft to the older Air Force One before leaving Ankara had raised questions over the security of the Qatari-donated plane.Trump had said on Truth Social before departing Ankara that he would use the older baby-blue Air Force One "for old time's sake" to fly to RAF Mildenhall in Britain, while the new aircraft would also stop at the same base so US service members stationed there could tour it.However, after Trump boarded the older aircraft in front of cameras, he was secretly transferred to the C-32A using an airport catering truck, according to the Post.The deception operation was triggered by a credible threat to Trump, the Post reported. A similar operation took place in 2000, when President Bill Clinton used an unmarked executive jet to fly into Pakistan while sending his formal Air Force One as a decoy.Also read: 'Blood for blood': Iran displays giant billboard with Donald, Melania and Trump children in coffins On this occasion, journalists who believed they were travelling with Trump aboard the older Air Force One were advised to keep their window shades in the press cabin closed. The Post reported that some White House staff also believed the president was on board.When reporters later asked Trump why they had been told to keep the shades shut during the flight, he said they were "probably on a dangerous flight." He went onto say: “But if I go, you go. Right?"The C-32A carrying Trump arrived in Britain at around 10:20 p.m., with the older Air Force One and media arriving minutes later, the Post reported. It was not immediately clear how Trump was transferred from the C-32A back to the older Air Force One.Trump's travelling press pool reported that he climbed down the stairs of the older Air Force One at 10:56 p.m. local time. He gave reporters a peace sign but did not walk over to speak with them.He then spent some time greeting US service members before walking towards the new Qatar-donated aircraft.Asked about the revelation that Trump had secretly travelled on a third aircraft, the White House provided a statement from Communications Director Steve Cheung saying the Qatari-donated jet had been fitted with high-level security protocols to protect the president and his staff."As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats," Cheung said.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump was secretly moved in an airport catering truck to a smaller military aircraft after boarding Air Force One in Ankara. The Washington Post reported that the operation was triggered by an Iranian assassination threat. The extraordinary security operation came as hostilities with Iran were escalating. Trump had said on Truth Social before departing Ankara that he would use the older aircraft "for old time's sake"

Article Title: Typhoon Dolphin batters China: Hundreds of flights cancelled, lakhs evacuated as floods hit east
Article Text:
The densely populated Chinese ​capital of Beijing ​braced for the expected onset ​of more than one-third of its annual rainfall over 24 hours

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is most important during extreme weather events? Early evacuation and safety measures Timely weather warnings and updates 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Typhoon Dolphin pushed deeper inland into China's central Hubei province on Tuesday, prompting the closure of tourist sites and suspension of high-risk construction projects. Forecasts warned of extreme rainfall, with flooding and landslides posing a risk across the province, as Chinese authorities evacuated more than a million people.China’s national meteorological center renewed an orange alert for heavy rain, the second-highest warning level, with northwestern Hubei expected to receive as much as 250 mm of rain in 24 hours. Authorities also issued a yellow warning for cities including Xiangyang, Huanggang and Suizhou.Hubei, a major hub for automobile and high-tech electronics manufacturing, is home to more than 58 million people. The province was hit by two rare tornadoes last month in the aftermath of Typhoon Maysak, which killed at least 11 people.The storm moved over a long distance of 6,000km before making landfall, suggesting a lifespan of more than three times that of an average typhoon, according to China's state broadcaster CCTV.Dolphin, the strongest typhoon to hit China this year, travelled nearly 6,000 km before making landfall over the weekend, drenching the country's eastern coast and carrying a sprawling cloud field inland, Reuters reported.Hubei authorities temporarily closed scenic areas, including the popular Three Gorges Dam tourist area in Yichang. Of 107 major highway and waterway construction projects under way across the province, 26 high-risk projects were suspended.The storm's effects are expected to extend more than 1,000 km north to Beijing. Four districts on the capital's outskirts activated Level I emergency flood responses as the city prepared for more than one-third of its annual rainfall in a 24-hour period from late Tuesday.Beijing's meteorological service forecast heavy rain across most of the capital from Tuesday evening through Thursday, with cumulative rainfall expected to exceed 100 mm in six hours and 150 mm in 24 hours. Some districts, including Tongzhou, Daxing, Fangshan, Mentougou, Huairou and Fengtai, could receive more than 200 mm in 24 hours.The storm is also being closely monitored in Japan. The Japan meteorological agency said Typhoon No. 15, Chan-hom, could move across mainland Japan, with authorities preparing for possible landslides, flooding and strong winds.
Article Summary: Typhoon Dolphin pushed deeper inland into China's central Hubei province on Tuesday, prompting the closure of tourist sites and suspension of high-risk construction projects. Forecasts warned of extreme rainfall, with flooding and landslides posing a risk across the province. China’s national meteorological center renewed an orange alert for heavy rain, the second-highest warning level.

Article Title: ‘We’re reducing them’: Trump targets childhood vaccine schedule, pushes separate MMR jabs
Article Text:
The order calls for childhood immunisations to be given at separate medical visits “to the maximum extent feasible”

Trump calls for fewer vaccines, separate appointments

Doctors warn of vaccination gaps

US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order seeking sweeping changes to the country’s childhood vaccination recommendations, including reducing the number of vaccines routinely recommended for children and separating combination shots into multiple appointments.The order calls for childhood immunisations to be given at separate medical visits “to the maximum extent feasible” and directs the US government to work towards making individual measles, mumps and rubella vaccines available. The move revives Trump’s long-standing claims about vaccine safety and autism, despite decades of research finding no evidence of a link between childhood vaccines and autism.The changes have drawn strong criticism from doctors and public health experts, who warn that spacing out vaccinations could leave children vulnerable to preventable diseases and make it harder for families to complete recommended immunisation schedules.Speaking at the signing ceremony, Trump said his administration was adopting “gold standard” recommendations covering 11 core diseases, down from 18 diseases covered by recommendations at the end of 2024.The vaccines continuing to have full recommendations cover measles, mumps, rubella, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, Haemophilus influenzae type B, pneumococcal disease, human papillomavirus and chickenpox.“We're reducing them,” Trump said. “It's not only that you're doing fewer vaccines, or jabs, as they say, but you're doing them in a series of visits to the doctor.”The order also seeks to split the combined MMR vaccine into three separate shots once individual vaccines become available in the US. Trump suggested the combined vaccine could be dangerous.“Together, there could be a possibility they’re quite lethal,” Trump said of the MMR vaccine at the signing of the order on Monday.However, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says there is “no published scientific evidence that shows any benefit in separating the combination MMR vaccine into three individual shots”. It also says getting the MMR vaccine is safer than contracting measles, mumps or rubella.Public health experts have raised concerns that requiring multiple appointments could increase the chances of children contracting vaccine-preventable diseases before receiving their next dose. Families could also be more likely to miss appointments when vaccinations are spread across several visits.Dr Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics, criticised the changes, saying they would create unnecessary uncertainty.“Science about vaccines and their efficacy has not changed,” he said. “The distribution of viruses and other pathogens in our environment has not changed. Children in this country have not changed in the last 48 hours."Republican Senator Bill Cassidy, a doctor and chair of the Senate health committee, also opposed the order.“I'm a doctor. This executive order is wrong,” the Louisiana senator wrote. “The President does not have the expertise to make these changes.”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order seeking sweeping changes to the country’s childhood vaccination recommendations. The order calls for childhood immunisations to be given at separate medical visits “to the maximum extent feasible” and directs the US government to work towards making individual measles, mumps and rubella vaccines available. Doctors and public health experts warn that spacing out vaccinations could leave children vulnerable to preventable diseases.

Article Title: More than 1,75,000 visas revoked so far in Trump's second term: Majority due to criminal activities, DUI
Article Text:
When the State Department revokes the legal status of migrants and deems them illegal, it is called visa revocation.

What is visa revocation ?

A foreign national who was charged with felony rape and sexual battery – including of a victim who was mentally disabled.

A foreign national charged with felony kidnapping, human trafficking, and sexual exploitation of a minor.

A foreign national arrested for disorderly conduct, resisting arrest with violence, drunk driving, and domestic violence.

A US embassy in North Africa revoked over 100 visas for “birth tourist” parents who came to the United States primarily to give birth so their children would get US citizenship.

A foreign national charged with sodomy of a child and aggravated sexual battery.

A foreign national charged with over a dozen counts of possessing child sexual abuse material.

A foreign national was arrested for driving with heroin and a blood alcohol level more than 3x the legal limit.

Multiple foreign nationals who celebrated the assassination of Charlie Kirk, including one who stated “when fascists die, democrats don’t complain” and another who said he “died too late.”

A foreign national who claimed to operate a legitimate business helping vulnerable patients access healthcare helped orchestrate a massive Medicaid scam – billing for over $5 million of fake services.

A foreign national built a company on lies – faking revenue and fooling investors to swindle millions of dollars from clients. The foreign national used the false claims and forged letters to fraudulently secure a visa.

A foreign national who came to the US to teach young students and was then arrested for sexually assaulting one.

From classrooms to careers, Trump tightens the immigration squeeze

The US State Department Monday published the exact number of visas revoked in the second term of Donald Trump's presidency. As per the data, US has revoked more than 1,75,000 visas from foreign nationals who violated the terms of their visas, committed crimes, called for violence against US citizens, defrauded Americans, abused our immigration system, or endangered national security, the department said."The majority of these visas were revoked due to law enforcement encounters for a range of criminal activity, with assault, driving under the influence, theft, and drug crimes being the leading causes. A significant share of visas were revoked for reckless driving, sexual assault, child abuse, fraud and embezzlement, and other crimes," the department said.When the State Department revokes the legal status of migrants and deems them illegal, it is called visa revocation. It is different from denaturalization as denaturalization happens only to those who have become US citizens.Secretary of State Marco Rubio has determined that numerous foreign nationals are deportable on foreign policy grounds, including a Cuban national connected to a Cuban communist regime influence operation, Iranian nationals with connections to the Iranian regime, a Laotian child sex offender pardoned by Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, and a Kuwaiti national who wished for violence against the President of the United States and called Americans his “enemy", the department said giving a list of other significant visa revocations."Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio’s leadership, the State Department will continue to identify, investigate, and revoke the visas of foreign nationals who threaten the safety of the American people. A US visa is a privilege, not a right. The Department remains committed to using every tool available to protect our communities from those who abuse it," the department said.Also read: Visa revocation, travel ban for reckless drivers: US says no second chance to those who put American lives at risk The Trump administration is tightening the immigration rules facing foreign talent at both ends of the pipeline, from international students to highly skilled workers. A new DHS rule will replace the current ‘duration of status’ system for F-1 students with fixed periods of stay, generally capped at four years, while cutting the post-study grace period from 60 days to 30.The rules also restrict students’ ability to change programmes or fields of study, particularly at graduate level, potentially adding costs, delays and uncertainty. At the other end, the administration is considering scrapping the 60-day grace period for H-1B workers who lose their jobs. For Indians, who make up the largest group of international students in the US and a major share of H-1B workers, the changes could make studying, working and building a long-term life in America significantly more difficult.
Article Summary: The US State Department Monday published the exact number of visas revoked in the second term of Donald Trump's presidency. US has revoked more than 1,75,000 visas from foreign nationals who violated the terms of their visas, committed crimes, called for violence against US citizens, defrauded Americans.

Article Title: Over 100 aides, journalists flew on as unwitting decoys after Trump secretly switched planes in Turkey
Article Text:
Trump secretly switched planes amid Iran threat, over 100 left onboard Air Force One

Following a Nato summit in Turkey, US President Donald Trump was secretly moved off Air Force One in an airport catering truck after US intelligence reportedly identified a credible Iranian plot to kill him last month, The Washington Post and The New York Times reported.More than 100 aides, officials and journalists remained aboard the aircraft and continued flying towards Britain, reportedly unaware of the threat that had prompted the covert security operation, as cited by the Guardian.Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut described the operation as “unprecedented and surreal” and “downright scary” in an interview with CNN.“There has to be a congressional briefing because it involves not just the safety of the president."“I want to know what precautions were taken to make sure that all of the passengers on that Air Force One, which was judged too dangerous for the president to fly on, what precautions were taken to keep the staff and reporters on that plane safe?” Blumenthal added.The White House had publicly announced that Trump would travel to Britain aboard Air Force One, although it would be the older aircraft rather than the newly refurbished Boeing 747 donated by Qatar.Trump initially boarded the presidential jet in full view of television cameras but was secretly transferred minutes later to an Air Force C-32A.The deception was elaborate enough that journalists travelling with the president, as well as some White House staff, believed Trump remained aboard Air Force One. Reporters were instructed to keep the window shades in the press cabin closed during the flight.The C-32A carrying Trump arrived at RAF Mildenhall in Britain at around 10.20 pm (local time), with the older Air Force One and the travelling press pool arriving minutes later. Photographers later captured Trump disembarking from the presidential aircraft, apparently after rejoining it.Trump then greeted troops at the base before boarding the newly refurbished Boeing 747 donated by Qatar and continuing his journey to Washington.US President Donald Trump has confirmed that he was secretly moved to another aircraft while leaving Turkey, saying he followed instructions from the Secret Service and military after being told that the plane he had initially boarded faced a “greater risk”."I go by Secret Service and the military. They wanted me to go on a different flight, a different plane... I do what they say... I guess there was a threat out there. I didn't really ask too much about it. I get a lot of threats," the US president said."I think actually the plane that I flew on was at greater risk! I think it was at greater risk because that would be the plane, I think that they would be more likely to go for it," Trump added.At the time, Trump said the newly refurbished aircraft was being flown to Mildenhall so US troops stationed there could inspect it. However, The New York Times and CBS News later reported that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a possible attack targeting Trump or his aircraft amid escalating tensions with Iran.During the Nato summit, the US military was also carrying out major strikes against Iran, heightening concerns about possible Iranian retaliation.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump was secretly moved off Air Force One in an airport catering truck after US intelligence reportedly identified a credible Iranian plot to kill him. More than 100 aides, officials and journalists remained aboard the aircraft and continued flying towards Britain. Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut described the operation as “unprecedented and surreal” and “downright scary”

Article Title: 'I go by Secret Service, military': Trump confirms switching planes in Turkey over Iran threat
Article Text:
Trump confirms secret flight switch

US president Donald Trump has acknowledged that he was moved to a different aircraft while leaving Turkey last month, saying he followed instructions from the Secret Service and military after being told the plane he had initially boarded would face a “greater risk”."I go by Secret Service and the military. They wanted me to go on a different flight, a different plane... I do what they say... I guess there was a threat out there. I didn't really ask too much about it. I get a lot of threats," the US president said."I think actually the plane that I flew on was at greater risk! I think it was at greater risk because that would be the plane, I think that they would be more likely to go for it," Trump added.His comments came after a Washington Post report revealed that Trump was secretly transferred from Air Force One to a smaller military aircraft in an airport catering truck amid an alleged Iranian assassination threat.Trump had initially boarded the older, baby-blue Air Force One in full view of cameras after attending the Nato summit in Turkey.Also read: Video shows catering truck used to secretly move Trump between planes amid Iran threat But once aboard, he was secretly transferred in an airport catering truck to an Air Force C-32A, which flew him to Britain, The Washington Post reported, citing a US official familiar with the operation and corroborating material reviewed by the newspaper.Israel had reportedly alerted the United States to the threat that prompted the Secret Service to move Trump off Air Force One and transfer him to a military aircraft as he prepared to leave Turkey, The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday, citing an unnamed US official.According to the report, Israeli intelligence indicated that Iran was planning to target Trump’s aircraft with shoulder-fired missiles. Despite the threat, several senior Trump administration officials, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio, remained aboard Air Force One, the official said.The extraordinary security operation unfolded as hostilities with Iran were escalating. Iran shares a border with Turkey, where Trump had travelled for the NATO summit and made his first international trip aboard a newly renovated aircraft donated by Qatar.The deception operation was triggered by what The Washington Post described as a credible threat to Trump. A similar tactic was used in 2000, when then-President Bill Clinton flew into Pakistan aboard an unmarked executive jet while the official Air Force One aircraft served as a decoy.In this case, journalists who believed they were travelling with Trump aboard the older Air Force One were instructed to keep the window shades in the press cabin closed. Some White House staff members also reportedly believed the president was on board.The C-32A carrying Trump arrived in Britain at around 10:20 pm (local time), with the older Air Force One and the media contingent arriving minutes later, The Post reported. It was not immediately clear how Trump was transferred back to the older Air Force One.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump says he followed instructions from the Secret Service and military. Trump was secretly transferred from Air Force One to a smaller military aircraft in an airport catering truck amid an alleged Iranian assassination threat. Israeli intelligence indicated that Iran was planning to target Trump’s aircraft with shoulder-fired missiles, The Washington Post reported.

Article Title: Chicago hit by severe storms as 500,000+ lose power, flights halted
Article Text:
The storms brought torrential rain and extreme winds, with a 99 mph (159 kph) gust recorded

Roofs torn off, roads flooded

Severe weather disrupts communities

Chicago and parts of the wider Midwest were hit by severe storms on Tuesday, leaving more than 500,000 customers without power, grounding flights and causing widespread damage across Illinois and north-western Indiana.Power outages affected more than 600,000 customers across Illinois and Indiana at the peak of the storm, according to PowerOutage.us, with Lake and Porter counties in Indiana and Will County south of Chicago among the hardest-hit areas. The storms also disrupted air travel, with all flights temporarily halted at Chicago’s two major airports as officials dealt with the dangerous conditions and worked to clear a backlog.The storms brought torrential rain and extreme winds, with a 99 mph (159 kph) gust recorded in Gary, Indiana. Numerous other locations reported winds of 80 mph (128 kph) or more.The National Weather Service’s Storm Prediction Center said preliminary information indicated that the system, which moved from Iowa into Indiana over several hours, qualified as a derecho – a widespread, long-lasting windstorm capable of producing damage comparable to that caused by tornadoes.The force of the storms was felt across the Chicago suburbs and into Indiana, where photos and videos showed fallen trees, flooded roads, debris and homes with sections of their roofs ripped away.At Midwest Animal Hospital in Orland Park, staff rushed to protect dozens of dogs after winds exceeding 70 mph began tearing parts of the veterinary hospital’s roof away. Footage showed damaged gutters, debris scattered across the property and pieces of wood hanging from dog kennels.The storm also caused leaks and flooding in the hospital’s pet daycare area. The hospital said its roof and daycare facility suffered significant damage and would require extensive repairs, although its main operations, appointments and emergency and urgent-care services were unaffected. All staff and animals were reported safe.The damage was also severe in Portage, Indiana, where the local police chief described the destruction as the worst he had seen from a single storm. Schools across parts of the Chicago area and north-western Indiana cancelled classes on Wednesday, with some warning that further disruptions could follow as crews assess damage and restore power.Residents described scenes of destruction and widespread power loss. In Homewood, Illinois, resident Javid Jenkins said he and his family took shelter in the basement as the storm passed.“We’re built for snow. We’re built for cold. We’re not built for this,” Jenkins said, adding that he was searching for petrol to run a generator and keep food from spoiling.The storms also affected Ohio, where nearly 290,000 customers were without electricity. In Roseville, one person died during a health emergency after flooding prevented first responders from reaching them, Ohio Governor Mike DeWine said.Dayton recorded 2.07 inches (5.25 cm) of rain in a single day, breaking a rainfall record set in 1915. Forecasters warned that further rounds of heavy rain could bring additional flooding across the Ohio Valley through early Friday.Officials continued to assess the damage as communities began clearing debris, restoring power and determining when schools and other services could safely reopen.
Article Summary: The storms brought torrential rain and extreme winds, with a 99 mph (159 kph) gust recorded in Gary, Indiana. Power outages affected more than 600,000 customers across Illinois and Indiana at the peak of the storm. The storms also disrupted air travel, with all flights temporarily halted at Chicago’s two major airports.

Article Title: Video shows catering truck used to secretly move Trump between planes amid Iran threat
Article Text:
The video shows the vehicle later leaving the plane and heading towards a smaller Air Force C-32A (Credit: CBS)

Air Force One became a decoy

Why the secret operation was unusual

A video has emerged showing the airport catering truck that was used to secretly move President Donald Trump between aircraft during a covert security operation in Turkey last month.The footage shows the truck pulling away from Air Force One shortly after Trump had boarded the presidential aircraft following the Nato summit in Ankara. Instead of remaining aboard the plane, Trump was secretly taken off through the catering vehicle and driven across the airport to a smaller US government aircraft. The operation allowed officials to make it appear that Trump was travelling on the presidential plane while he was, in fact, aboard another aircraft.Trump eventually flew to Britain aboard the smaller plane before secretly rejoining the presidential aircraft there. The operation, first reported by The Washington Post and later confirmed by other US media, has raised questions about the nature of the threat against Trump and the lengths officials were prepared to go to conceal his movements.Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard a luxury aircraft gifted to the US by Qatar, which was expected to eventually serve as Air Force One.However, concerns had been raised about the aircraft's security capabilities because it was still being retrofitted and did not have some of the missile-detection and countermeasure systems found on older presidential aircraft.During the trip, officials announced that Trump would leave Turkey aboard an older presidential aircraft. That announcement appears to have been part of the deception.After Trump boarded the older plane, a catering truck approached the aircraft. The video shows the vehicle later leaving the plane and heading towards a smaller Air Force C-32A, a government aircraft commonly used for presidential travel. Trump was secretly transferred to the C-32A, while the aircraft he had initially boarded remained part of the operation.The Qatari aircraft, the older presidential plane and the C-32A then departed separately for Britain. Trump travelled aboard the C-32A and, after arriving in the UK, secretly transferred back to the Qatari aircraft before continuing his journey home.The move meant that White House officials, security personnel, support staff and members of the press travelling with Trump on the presidential aircraft were unknowingly aboard what effectively became a decoy plane.The White House has not directly confirmed the details of the operation, but it has not denied reports that the elaborate measures were prompted by an Iranian threat. White House communications director Steven Cheung said the president's aircraft had high-level security protocols and that officials use "every tool at our disposal" to address threats against Trump.Presidents have previously used decoy aircraft, undisclosed routes and surprise overseas trips when travelling to dangerous areas. Trump himself made a secret visit to Afghanistan in 2019, while George W. Bush made an undisclosed trip to Iraq in 2003 and Barack Obama travelled secretly to Afghanistan in 2010.Joe Biden also travelled secretly to Ukraine in 2023, taking a government aircraft to Poland before boarding an overnight train to Kyiv. A small number of journalists accompanied him and were able to document the visit once it was under way.There have also been previous instances of presidents switching aircraft. During Bill Clinton's 2000 trip from India to Pakistan, reporters knew he would not be travelling on the aircraft they were initially watching, although they were not told which plane he would use.The Turkey operation was different because the press travelling with Trump was apparently unaware that the president had left their aircraft. The deception also remained undisclosed for weeks, meaning there was a period during which the travelling press corps could not independently verify Trump's location.The operation also revived questions about the security of the Qatari aircraft that Trump has promoted as a future Air Force One. While officials have described it as highly capable, concerns over its retrofitting and defensive systems were reportedly a factor in the decision to use another aircraft for Trump's immediate departure from Turkey.
Article Summary: Video shows truck pulling away from Air Force One shortly after Trump had boarded the presidential aircraft following the Nato summit in Ankara. Instead of remaining aboard the plane, Trump was secretly taken off through the catering vehicle and driven across the airport to a smaller US government aircraft. The operation allowed officials to make it appear that Trump was travelling on the presidential plane while he was, in fact, aboard another aircraft.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Peter Thiel: 'First mover advantage is a trap, it's much better to be the last mover'
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Peter Thiel.

First mover advantage

is a trap; it's much better to be the last mover'

What is first-mover advantage?

How to be a last-mover?

PayPal founder Peter Thiel contradicted the well-known business lesson that being the first mover in a sector has its own advantage and suggested that it is highly overrated and a trap. Because first-movers can become unseated by a new entrant and he supported his theory by citing how Microsoft remained the last operating system for a long time, Google the last search engine for a long time and neither first mover. Thiel presented this idea on several occasions: in his speeches and books, and said, '. While starting early might generate temporary buzz, it rarely creates lasting value, he believes. What actually matters in business is not who enters the arena first, but who stays there last. In Thiel's view, the ultimate goal of any ambitious startup is not to be a pioneer, but to become the last mover in its category -- the company that makes the final major breakthrough and secures an unassailable monopoly for decades to come.The conventional wisdom in Silicon Valley has long celebrated the first-mover advantage.Business schools and startup incubators frequently teach that getting to a market first allows a company to capture brand recognition, secure early customers, and set the standards for an entire industry. Thiel rejects this premise as a dangerous distraction. Being first, he points out, often means absorbing massive research and development costs, educating a skeptical consumer base, and making critical strategic mistakes that later competitors can analyze and avoid for free. A first mover clears the path, but a fast follower with a better business model usually captures the rewards.To illustrate this point, Thiel points to the history of the technology industry, which is littered with the forgotten remains of first movers. Netscape was the first modern web browser, but Internet Explorer and Google Chrome eventually wiped it out. Myspace and Friendster were the first major social networks, but Facebook displaced them entirely. AltaVista and Yahoo were the early leaders in web search, but Google redefined the category with a far superior algorithm. In each case, the first mover did the hard labor of proving that a market existed, only to be overtaken by a later entrant that executed better, scaled faster, and built a vastly superior product.Thiel argues that a company's true economic value resides entirely in its future cash flows. If a startup generates impressive revenues for five years but gets disrupted and erased by a competitor in year six, its long-term value is remarkably low. Conversely, if a company can achieve dominance and maintain it for twenty or thirty years without being displaced, its value becomes almost immeasurable. This is why being the last mover is so critical. A last mover enters a market, makes the definitive technical or operational leap, builds deep competitive moats, and permanently shuts out future competitors.Thiel outlines a specific, step-by-step framework that runs counter to standard growth strategies.First, startups should avoid targeting massive, broadly defined markets from day one. When a founder claims they are going to capture just one percent of a hundred-billion-dollar market, Thiel sees a major red flag. Large markets mean fierce competition, slim profit margins, and constant price wars that burn through capital. Instead, a startup should aim to dominate a very small, tightly defined niche where it can quickly capture eighty or ninety percent market share.PayPal did not start by trying to revolutionize global payments for everyone. It focused exclusively on a tiny subset of users: high-volume power sellers on eBay who desperately needed a faster way to process payments. By solving that specific problem better than anyone else, PayPal captured that small niche completely. Only after dominating eBay payments did the company expand into broader financial services. Similarly, Facebook did not launch as a global network for billions of people. It launched exclusively for Harvard undergraduate students. Once Mark Zuckerberg achieved near-total adoption within that single campus, he expanded to other Ivy League schools, then to all universities, and finally to the general public.Second, to ensure that no latecomer can displace you once you dominate a niche, Thiel emphasizes the need to build durable economic moats. The most powerful of these is proprietary technology. A company's core technology must be at least ten times better than its closest substitute to create a true last-mover advantage. An improvement of ten percent or twenty percent is easily copied or bypassed, but a tenfold improvement makes the competition obsolete. Google’s early search algorithm was not just slightly better than Yahoo’s; it was orders of magnitude faster and more accurate, making it nearly impossible for users to switch back.Ultimately, Thiel’s philosophy on the last mover is a challenge to how founders think about competition and innovation. Being first might gain headlines, but being last builds an empire. The real winners in business are not the speed demons who sprint out of the gate, but the strategists who design a product so complete, so dominant, and so hard to replicate that no one ever needs to build a better version again.
Article Summary: Peter Thiel: Being the first mover in a sector is highly overrated and a trap. Being first often means absorbing massive research and development costs, educating a skeptical consumer base, and making critical strategic mistakes that later competitors can analyze and avoid for free. Thiel argues that a company's true economic value resides entirely in its future cash flows.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Bloomberg: 'I'm not smarter than anybody else but I can outwork you', and a controversial career advice
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael Bloomberg.

"I'm not smarter than anybody else, but I can outwork you,"

Who is Michael Bloomberg ?

Fired from Salomon Brothers when he was 39

Don't take vacation: Bloomberg's controversial career advice

Inspiring take but controversial today

In a professional world caught between working smart and working hard, Michael Bloomberg always maintained that he favored hard work because he was no genius. Today, this stands as a controversial piece of advice, but it remains the core principle that sustained his business career and his time in public office. When he made his famous statement at a TechCrunch event in 2011, he was not just a billionaire CEO; he was actively serving as the mayor of New York City.he said, crediting this exact mindset for taking him from a low-level desk job on Wall Street to founding a global financial media company and serving three terms as NYC mayor.Bloomberg's belief in hard work started in the late 1960s at the Wall Street investment bank Salomon Brothers. When he arrived, the company was full of smart graduates from famous Ivy League schools. Bloomberg knew his grades were average and that he could not beat these people on raw intellect alone. He realized that the only thing he could control was how many hours he put in every day. He decided to arrive at the office before everyone else and stay long after everyone had gone home.In those days, the head of the firm and the top partners arrived at six in the morning.Since Bloomberg was already at his desk, he was the only person around to buy them coffee, hand over trade papers, or take on extra chores. That early arrival gave him direct access to the most powerful people in the company. By the time the rest of the staff walked in at eight in the morning, Bloomberg had already spent two hours talking with the bosses and learning how the business ran. He used that exact same routine for years, outworking his peers until he became a partner at the firm.Despite his hard work, Bloomberg was fired from Salomon Brothers at age thirty-nine in 1981. But he did not complain or take a break. He took his severance money, bought a few computers, and started his own business selling financial information to Wall Street banks. The market was already dominated by big, established companies, but Bloomberg applied his usual strategy. He worked seven days a week, made sales calls himself, and spent endless hours refining his products. His firm grew into a multi-billion-dollar global company, Bloomberg L.P., simply because he refused to slow down or let competitors catch up to him."I always tried to be the first person in the office in the morning and the last one to leave at night, and I took as little vacation as possible," Bloomberg explained when describing how he built his edge. During his early days at Salomon Brothers, staying late was how he built relationships with decision-makers: "If [the partner] needed to borrow a match... if he wanted to ask something about a newspaper or a stock, he came over and so we became buddies. ""You can't control that you're the smartest guy. There'll always be somebody smarter. But if you're there, then you absorb things. You put things together in ways that if you didn't have all that experience...""Reading a book on skiing doesn't teach you how to ski. You got to go and you got to ski and get lots of miles under your skis. And incidentally, if you don't fall, you're not skiing hard enough and you're not learning anything.""You got to be smart enough to say, 'Hey, I tried it. Don't let your ego get in the way. I can't keep doing this. I've got to earn a living, but a year from now, I'm going to come up with a better idea and then I'll go back and do it again.'""There's never been a day that I haven't looked forward to going into work. Even the days I knew I was going to get beaten up. Even the day I knew I was going to get fired. I'd never been fired before. I wonder what it's like. Okay, let's go find out."That advice runs directly against what most modern workplace experts teach today. Critics argue that telling employees to avoid vacations is a fast track to physical exhaustion, mental health problems, and severe burnout. They point out that working endlessly does not mean you are doing good work, because tired people make mistakes and lose creative thinking power. In a modern corporate world that values mental health, flexible work options, and personal well-being, Bloomberg’s views sound harsh, outdated, and unreasonable to many workers.But Bloomberg made it clear that he does not care about those complaints. He does not view work as something that should be easy or comfortable. To him, the corporate world is a tough arena where only the most dedicated people reach the top. He often says that if you genuinely enjoy your career, you will not feel a strong need to take a break from it. He also advises managers to give important assignments to the busiest, most overworked people in the building, because he believes busy people are the only ones who know how to manage time efficiently and get things done.There is a clear honesty to Bloomberg’s perspective, even if many people dislike it. He does not pretend that building massive wealth and power is easy, nor does he pretend you can achieve great things while maintaining a balanced life. He presents a very clear choice: if you want ordinary results, you can work ordinary hours, but if you want extraordinary success, you have to sacrifice your time, comfort, and personal life. Whether you view his ideas as a solid guide to winning or a dangerous recipe for burnout, his life proves one fundamental point. In his world, showing up early and staying late matters far more than being the smartest person in the room.
Article Summary: Michael Bloomberg: "I'm not smarter than anybody else, but I can outwork you" "I always tried to be the first person in the office in the morning and the last one to leave at night" "There's never been a day that I haven't looked forward to going into work" "Don't let your ego get in the way. I can't keep doing this. I've got to earn a living"

Article Title: In 1929, a Tennessee farmer refused $20 an acre for 375 acres wanted for Great Smoky Mountains National Park; after years in court, he received $17,000 and lost the farm
Article Text:
