In a significant public admission by terrorist organisation Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), senior commander Rizwan Hanif has claimed that over 30 members linked to the group have been killed across Pakistani cities since 2020 by "India agents". LeT members were targeted in Peshawar, Karachi, Rawalpindi, Muzaffarabad and Rawalakot, Hanif said while addressing a crowd in Pakistan.Attempting to frame these targeted killings as religious persecution, Hanif - the wanted deputy chief of Lashkar's POK unit - launched into inflammatory rhetoric. In a video circulated on social media, he questioned the group's "crime", asserting they were targeted solely for their faith.Hanif also launched a sharp attack against other faiths in his speech which was filmed by his followers and uploaded on social media.He declared that the outfit would continue its activities, rejecting the authority of foreign powers, including the US and Israel.The hate-filled speech comes on the heels of Lt General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, the official spokesperson of Pakistan armed forces (DG-ISPR), and the son of a US-designated terrorist peddling similar extremist views on a video while alleging that Afghans were not Muslims.Security experts saw these speeches as a face-saving narrative building exercise. The escalation in sectarian rhetoric comes as Islamabad faces mounting public unrest in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir, where violent state crackdowns against anti-govt protesters at Rawalakot, in particular, and other places have drawn severe criticism while denting Pakistan's narrative about it being the champion of Kashmiris and their right to self-determination.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif also labelled anti-govt demonstrators in POK as "enemies" comparable to India and ruled out any dialogue with them while defending the violent attacks on protesters.
Article Summary: Rizwan Hanif, a commander affiliated with Lashkar-e-Taiba, has alleged that Indian agents have systematically killed more than thirty individuals in different Pakistani locations since 2020. He characterized these murders as acts of religious persecution and rejected the authority of foreign entities. This statement comes amid heightened rhetoric from Pakistan's military, and experts suggest it serves as a strategic narrative.

Article Title: ‘Hasina will get full security if she returns’: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman’s adviser
Article Text:
Addressing a press conference in New Delhi on August 5, Hasina said she was not afraid of being arrested if she returned to Bangladesh.

DHAKA: A day after protesting to New Delhi against Sheikh Hasina ’s continuing exile in India, Bangladesh govt Tuesday promised the former PM “full security” if she returns, while leaving it to the courts to decide her future.“Hasina has said she will return home in Dec. When she returns home, she will be given full security and will be made to face judicial process with all kinds of rights — legal and constitutional — ensured. Then, everyone will have to accept the decision that the court gives,” PM’s information and broadcasting adviser Zahed Ur Rahman said.He said civil and constitutional rights of even those accused of the most serious crimes (during the 2024 uprising against Hasina govt), whether it is Shakib Al Hasan — former Awami League MP and Bangladesh cricketer— or Hasina, will be ensured, even as the adviser dubbed the former cricket star a “rotten man”.“We do not want to see a mafia regime like Hasina in this country again. We will not allow this to happen in the future, not a fascist mafia regime. This is a democratic state,” Zahed said.After Hasina’s Aug 5 virtual presser in New Delhi — where she declared she was not scared of being arrested upon her return — Bangladesh foreign ministry had called her a “convicted genocider”, a term foreign minister Khalilur Rahman, Zahed and other govt officials and ministers have refrained from using in news conferences thereafter.On a visit by a RAW delegation led by its chief Parag Jain to Dhaka, Zahed said it was part of a routine engagement between the two countries, “No Indian agency or institution will be allowed to operate freely in Bangladesh under the current govt as they did during the tenure of Hasina.”He said Jain’s visit was similar to the recent visit to India by the chief of Bangladesh’s directorate general of forces intelligence. “I see huge speculation, he (RAW chief) came from China. There is nothing to speculate. Our security issues can be there and discussion can be there too,” said the adviser.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has said she will return home in Dec. She said she was not afraid of being arrested if she returned to Bangladesh. PM’s information and broadcasting adviser Zahed Ur Rahman said civil and constitutional rights of even those accused of the most serious crimes will be ensured.

Article Title: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman raises Hasina extradition with Indian envoy
Article Text:
Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman (L) with Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi in Dhaka Monday

DHAKA: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman Monday raised the issue of the extradition of exiled Awami League leader and ex-PM Sheikh Hasina with Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi, emphasising that Dhaka was hopeful of a positive response, while cautioning India against "actions" that could hurt bilateral ties.Briefing reporters, foreign minister Khalilur Rahman, who was present at the "courtesy meeting", said Bangladesh wants all countries to respect the entire structure of the State, adding that "I believe India has understood Bangladesh's concerns". PM Tarique's advice that India should avoid actions that can hit ties was being seen as referring to Hasina's defiant virtual news conference last week in Delhi. "What Hasina did on Aug 5 was. ..she showed disrespect to the judiciary, one of the pillars of the State... and the Indian govt allowed that (news conference) to happen," said Khalilur."My impression, after speaking with them, is that they have understood it. We hope they will not do anything to undermine any pillar of our State again. This is our expectation, and based on my conversations with them, I am somewhat reassured that this incident will not be repeated," he further said of the Aug 5 presser by Hasina.In a statement, Bangladesh PM's office said the meeting between Tarique and Trivedi also "covered a range of important bilateral issues". The Indian high commission in Dhaka said Trivedi conveyed greetings from PM Narendra Modi and "the intent to work together with govt and people of Bangladesh in a positive, constructive and forward-looking manner."Bangladesh has also urged "India to hand over the suspected killers of Osman Hadi as early as possible", said Khalilur. In March, West Bengal Police arrested two Bangladeshis accused of his murder in the Indian town of Bongaon.Meanwhile, RAW chief Parag Jain arrived in Dhaka Sunday, reportedly as part of efforts to normalise ties between the two countries.
Article Summary: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman meets Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi in Dhaka. Rahman raises issue of extradition of exiled Awami League leader and ex- PM Sheikh Hasina. Foreign minister Khalilur Rahman: Bangladesh wants all countries to respect the entire structure of the State.

Article Title: Balen ends 'envoy snub' with India-first reset; meets China envoy within hours
Article Text:
Indian envoy Naveen Srivastava and Nepal PM Balen Shah discuss 'bilateral cooperation and development partnership'

NEW DELHI: Nepal PM Balendra Shah on Monday ended his self-imposed bar on one-on-one meetings with Kathmandu-based foreign envoys, receiving Indian ambassador Naveen Srivastava first and Chinese ambassador Zhang Maoming hours later at Singha Durbar in a diplomatic reset after months of a distancing that had increasingly come into question in Kathmandu and beyond. Shah is scheduled to meet US Embassy chargé d’affaires Scott Urbom on Tuesday extending the outreach beyond Nepal’s two neighbours.Shah and Srivastava discussed bilateral ties, mutual interests, development partnership and cooperation, with Shah stressing the need to deepen Nepal’s “historic relationship” with India. PMO said on social media that the talks focused on “further strengthening Nepal-India relations”, bilateral cooperation and development partnership.Srivastava said on X that he conveyed “warm greetings from Prime Minister Modi ji” and described the meeting as an “engaging & productive exchange” to deepen the “robust, multi-faceted India-Nepal partnership”. Neither side disclosed whether specific issues such as the boundary dispute, power trade or Shah’s proposed India visit figured in the talks.The India-first sequencing was significant. A senior foreign ministry official had told a Kathmandu-based daily before the meetings, “The Indian ambassador is told to come first, followed by the Chinese ambassador,” adding that the timing reflected govt’s foreign-policy priority.The two meetings had initially been planned about two weeks ago but were deferred after communal violence in Sunsari and other districts.Monday’s exchanges also contrasted with friction during Shah’s first weeks in office. His administration strictly enforced customs duties on low-value goods brought from India and protested to both New Delhi and Beijing over resumption of the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage through Lipulekh, which Nepal claims. Shah also refused to meet Indian foreign secretary Vikram Misri on protocol grounds. Misri’s planned May 11-12 Kathmandu visit was subsequently postponed.The reset came with Shah’s first India visit as PM still pending. Modi invited him soon after the latter took office on March 27 and Shah accepted, but no date has been fixed. India formally reiterated on July 28 that the invitation remained open.RSP president Rabi Lamichhane had received unusually high-profile treatment during his five-day India visit in June. BJP welcomed Lamichhane with a floral shower at its headquarters, where party president Nitin Nabin received him, before he met PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and NSA Ajit Doval. The reception drew attention because Shah’s govt had described Lamichhane’s trip as “a purely personal trip”.The stakes for the Himalayan nation extend beyond protocol: India accounts for over 60% of Nepal’s trade and almost all its third-country transit, while Shah’s govt has simultaneously sought greater Chinese investment, technology and tourism. Foreign minister Shisir Khanal has described India as a major potential market for Nepal’s electricity and China as an important source of tourists.
Article Summary: Nepal PM Balendra Shah ended his self-imposed bar on one-on-one meetings with Kathmandu-based foreign envoys. He received Indian ambassador Naveen Srivastava first and Chinese ambassador Zhang Maoming hours later at Singha Durbar. Shah is scheduled to meet US Embassy chargé d’affaires Scott Urbom on Tuesday.
